title: Attributional Safety Failures in Large Language Models under Code-Mixed Perturbations

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of models generating harmful content when presented with code-mixed prompts (blending English with 10 different matrix languages like Hindi, Arabic, and Bengali) compared to monolingual English prompts. The study also uses Saliency Drift Attribution (SDA) to visualize how model attention on safety-critical tokens degrades under code-mixed linguistic perturbations.

Evaluating model safety guardrails using a 'Local TestSet' consisting of culture-specific unsafe prompts tailored to 10 different cultural contexts. This tests whether models maintain safety alignment when faced with nuanced, regional sensitivities (e.g., caste-based discrimination in Hindi contexts or religious marginalization in Arabic contexts) as opposed to universally recognized harms.
